AK-2025-SB237.aiSummary: The law lets the state issue electronic ID cards, driver’s licenses, and permits on a mobile device to people who already have the physical card or license. It also sets rules for how police and other public safety staff can check them, including limits on searching the phone and protections for damage claims unless there is intentional misconduct. AK-2025-SB174.aiSummary: Would create the Alaska Invasive Species Council in the Department of Fish and Game to help state, tribal, local, and other groups work together on invasive species. The council would advise on how to manage these species, issue yearly reports and a five-year plan, and oversee a response fund for invasive species work. Members would serve without pay, and the bill would take effect right away if it became law.

AK-2025-SB3002.aiSummary: The bill would end Alaska income tax rules for pass-through businesses by repealing the current tax law for them on January 1, 2028. It would affect pass-through entities, such as some partnerships and S corporations, that report income through their owners.

AK-2025-HB3001.title: An Act relating to the taxation of certain natural gas project property and related facilities; relating to local contributions for public school funding; relating to municipal property taxes; relating to the Alaska Gasline Development Corporation and funds of the Alaska Gasline Development Corporation; relating to reporting requirements for natural gas pipeline projects; creating the Alaska affordable heating fuel fund; relating to approval of contracts by the Regulatory Commission of Alaska and inflation adjustment of the maximum price of natural gas; relating to an alternative volumetric tax on natural gas throughput; relating to a municipal impact grant program and fund; relating to agreements and a payment related to a natural gas project; and providing for an effective date.
AK-2025-HB3001.aiSummary: This bill would change tax rules for certain natural gas project property and related facilities, and it would set rules for a natural gas project’s ties to local school funding and city taxes. It would also change reporting rules for pipeline projects, create an affordable heating fuel fund, and create a municipal impact grant program and fund. The bill would also address Alaska Gasline Development Corporation funds, contract approval by the state utility commission, and a possible alternative tax on natural gas flow, and it includes an effective date.
